title: Why buyer-level marginal rates are not out-of-sample testable on this holdout
finding: Checksum-valid SIRET availability is a buyer-level property: in the real corpus, 27% of buyers never publish one and 5% always do. Splitting on buyer key therefore splits that property too, and the two real sides have genuinely different marginal rates (0.2993 calibration vs 0.1976 holdout, a 10.2 pp difference). A generator calibrated to the calibration side must differ from the holdout side by about that amount; the observed synthetic-versus-holdout gap of roughly +9.3 pp is almost exactly this, not a transfer failure.
consequence: This holdout provides genuine out-of-sample evidence for distributional-shape metrics -- within-SIREN name similarity, publication-year composition, candidate-count shape, activity quantiles -- because those are not induced by which buyers are in the split. It does NOT provide an out-of-sample test of buyer-level marginal rates (SIRET presence, SIREN presence, and to a lesser extent CPV missingness), which are confounded with the split by construction. Those metrics are reported as in-sample only.
alternative_considered: A notice-level split would leave the marginals comparable but would put the same buyer on both sides, which destroys the out-of-sample property for every within-buyer statistic -- including the buyer-name variation this revision exists to fix. The buyer-level split was kept and its limitation stated rather than trading away the evidence that matters most.
